source.title: Beware of Your Po! Measuring and Mitigating AI Safety Risks in Role-Play Fine-Tuning of LLMs
source.authors: Weixiang Zhao; Yu-Lin Hu; Yang Deng; Jiahe Guo; Xing-Yu Sui; Xin-Yang Han; An Zhang; Yan-Yan Zhao; Bing Qin; Tat-Seng Chua; Ting Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some appendix tables have flattened or visibly corrupted numbers; the rows below use clearly attributable values from the main tables and text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests safety changes from role-play fine-tuning, a distinct fine-tuning setting, and evaluates refusal under a jailbreak suite. It does not reproduce the original harmful-example fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper tests role-play fine-tuning and reports refusal rates on harmful-query benchmarks and an aggregate jailbreak measure. Table 2 also reports the effect of an explicitly unsafe system prompt; that result is recorded as related but not as a test of a listed claim version. Role-play scores and descriptions of cited prior findings are not recorded as safety rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained instruct models on benign RoleBench role-play data and reports GPT-4o-judged refusal rates on AdvBench, BeaverTails and HEx-PHI before and after. That bears directly on V2 in a new setting (role-play SFT). No other version is tested as such.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Role-play fine-tuning improves role-play but significantly lowers safety, especially for villainous or extreme characters. SaRFT (role-adaptive data selection via implicit reward, plus a KL loss on the selected subset) outperforms the baselines under LoRA and full fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: Role-play fine-tuning on RoleBench, evaluated with refusal rates on harmful-query benchmarks and an aggregate jailbreak suite; not a reproduction of harmful-example fine-tuning or token-position KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by backbone, full-parameter versus LoRA tuning, and evaluation benchmark; jailbreak-suite results also vary by model and tuning setting.

fits_no_version.finding: An explicitly unsafe role-play system prompt lowered BeaverTails refusal from 91.40 to 63.30 on LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsafe system-prompt instructions reduce refusal in safety-trained models.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The reported refusal rates are judged by GPT-4o; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The main results are averages across roles, and the paper notes that its largest model is 9B. The jailbreak results are aggregate scores rather than isolated measurements for each attack in these main tables.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant quantitative refusal rows were left out. Decoding-defense comparisons and SaRFT results are not recorded as tests of the claim's bypass or safety-depth versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or response-position analysis.

Jailbreaks (GCG, AIM, AutoDAN, Cipher, CodeChameleon) serve only as an evaluation suite. There is no prefill or decoding-attack test, and the original-model jailbreak numbers are not framed as a test of bypass. ROSE and Self-CD are safety defenses.
Not tested. SPPFT and SafeLoRA are run as baselines, but localization is not examined.
No test of what causes shallowness.
SaRFT's KL loss on selected data is a mitigation, but depth beyond the first tokens is not measured.

missing.what: Per-role refusal rates after SFT (e.g., Freddy Krueger 23.50, Gaston 44.70, Hawking 88.90, Catherine 94.00), showing role-trait dependence of benign-fine-tuning degradation
Per-attack jailbreak refusal before and after SFT (e.g., LLaMA full: AIM, AutoDAN, Cipher, CodeChameleon, GCG). These are needed to separate attack-specific rises from drops.

record.verdict_notes: The record's double labelling of the same row group as both supports and limits_scope has been replaced with condition-split labels. Jailbreak rows were moved off V4: they measure fine-tuning's effect on jailbreak compliance, not whether getting past the opening bypasses refusal. All refusal judgments come from GPT-4o, with no uncertainty reported. Tables 3/6 average 10 roles; Table 1 averages 95 roles.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is reported.
Tests RoleBench role-play fine-tuning, not ordinary general instruction data or a separate controlled comparison of benign datasets.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position measurement is reported.

Reports aggregate safety results over a jailbreak suite, not separate results for each suffix attack; does not test compliant-opening prefills. The decoding-based methods compared are safety defenses, not tests of decoding changes that bypass refusal.
No experiment identifies a small set of safety-carrying weights or ranks.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes token-depth shallowness.
SaRFT uses a KL loss on selected data, but the study does not measure whether safety is spread beyond early response tokens or whether such depth holds up.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma-2-9B full-parameter SFT, and all three models under LoRA SFT, harmful-query benchmarks
relationships.reason: Refusal still falls but by much less: about 6–7 points for Gemma full and 9–14 points under LoRA (r6–r20). The effect size depends on model and tuning method.
relationships.display_finding: Refusal on harmful-query benchmarks still fell, but by much less: about 6–7 points for Gemma full SFT and 9–14 points under LoRA, so effect size depends on model and tuning method.

relationships.reason: Jailbreak refusal falls sharply only for LLaMA full (r21) and slightly for LLaMA and Gemma LoRA (r24, r26). It rises for Qwen full and LoRA and Gemma full (r22, r23, r25), which the authors attribute to lost cipher/code comprehension.
relationships.display_finding: Jailbreak refusal fell sharply only for LLaMA full SFT and slightly for LLaMA and Gemma LoRA; it rose for Qwen full and LoRA and for Gemma full, which the authors attribute to lost cipher and code comprehension.

relation.reason: The study directly measures changes in safety following role-play fine-tuning of aligned models.

tranche.reason: Role-specific RoleBench fine-tuning is a new setting with before/after refusal measurements bearing directly on V2.

source_check.notes: The metric is GPT-4o-judged explicit refusal, not independently verified harmful-answer success. Table 1 averages 95 roles; Tables 3 and 6 average 10; the cipher/code explanation is the authors' proposed interpretation.

statements.correction: Table 3: Gemma full SFT AdvBench refusal 99.42→93.12; LLaMA full SFT 98.46→76.40. Jailbreak-average refusal: Qwen full 45.60→47.34; Gemma full 30.40→35.94. §4.2: authors suggest disrupted encrypted-text and code interpretation explains improved resistance to Cipher and CodeChameleon.
statements.problem: The numbers and proposed cipher/code explanation are accurate. However, retained refusal and a smaller decline do not challenge V2, which claims increased harmful compliance rather than complete removal of refusal. Only the reversed jailbreak results provide counterevidence in their particular settings.
